Subject: Synchronous inference pathways & deployment checklist — follow up

Alex — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Below is a concise recap of what we heard and the proposed checklist so we can size and scope a technical deep-dive next week. Please flag anything we miss.

Quick recap of pain & goals
- Primary pain: unpredictable tail-latency on peak inference which causes timeouts for live chat and UX errors.
- Goal: guarantee fast interactive responses for short prompts (<=256 tokens) while supporting longer background batches for analytics.
- Business metric: maintain 95th percentile latency <=200ms for interactive flows and 99th <=350ms; sustain peak concurrent throughput of ~400 req/s during business hours with bursts to 800 for short periods.

Key constraints we captured
- Model: production will use a 13B dense decoder model (your preference was to evaluate Llama3-13B-v2 and an xformers-optimized 13B variant). You also mentioned a fallback to a 6B distilled variant for cost-sensitive fallthroughs.
- Data residency: customer-managed VPC; logs retained per our SOC2 config (30 days standard, extended retention optional).
- Integration: REST/websocket API into your chat layer; deterministic prompt templating.

Preliminary topology & recommendations (high level)
- Deployment class: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) in two AZs for zone-failover.
- Warm pool sizing: min 4 replicas (2/zone) for low-latency steady-state; autoscale to max 24 GPUs for burst windows.
- Latency engineering: continuous batching for long-form work, but synchronous single-request fast-path with KV prefix caching and short-context kernel that prioritizes single-token generation hot path. Expect ~10–15% latency improvement from prefix cache on chat workflows.
- Fallback routing: policy-based routing to quantized 13B (INT8) and 6B distilled model when capacity constrained.

Questions / open items for the deep-dive
1) Can you share a 24h qps profile (CSV of minute-level req/s) and a small sample of median/95/99 latency traces? (we've attached a template to the drive link).
2) Do you have any hard SLA windows (e.g., support hours where latency SLO must be stricter)?
3) Expected procurement timeline for dedicated capacity and any internal procurement contacts (we've cc'd procurement above if different).

Attachments included: sagitta_mpa_draft.pdf (MPA draft), latency_characterization.csv (sample template), redwood-deploy-sketch.png (initial topology sketch).

Next steps / mutual action items
- We propose a technical deep-dive on Mon/Tue next week focused on: workload profile, exact model variant, KV caching strategy, warm-pool sizing, and failover policy.
- We'll produce a preliminary capacity model (GPU count estimate + cost ranges) within 48 hours after the deep-dive.
- We'll circulate a short MPA draft for signature that covers reserved capacity start/end dates.

If that all looks correct, please reply with availability and ownership for procurement / SRE so we can lock attendees.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad

Quick technical notes before Tuesday's deep-dive — filing these so the team has context:

- Model memory & kv-cache impact: Llama3-13B-v2 + 8k context with KV caching will increase per-replica memory by ~10–15% due to cached attention states. We'll include alternative kernel configs to trade memory for throughput.
- Warm pool strategy: recommend staggered warm-ups (start 60s before business-hour predicted spikes) and a minimal keep-alive to avoid cold-starts for the interactive fast-path.
- Autoscale: target scale-up latency for adding new replicas should be tested end-to-end; we typically recommend pre-warmed buffer replicas (the 4-replica min) to avoid reactive scale-up tails.
- Observability hooks: we'll push a small tracing slice that captures token-level latency and per-request routing decisions so your SREs can validate fallbacks.

I've attached a short CSV that shows the type of minute-level traffic profile we need (latency_characterization.csv). Marcus — can you draft a quick sketch of how we'd map your current API gateway to our routing policies?

-rishi
